tasks.name: diagnose-signal-biases
tasks.scopedGoal:
Quantify the signal/stability biases that the project's TODO list (see `outputs/report5.md` 'TODO (Next)') flagged: verdict bias, parse bias, unanimity bias, sampling-group effects, and verifier-vs-oracle drift. Use the existing rollout JSONLs already committed under `outputs/pairwise_rollouts_debug/` (do NOT re-run any GPU rollout). Add a new diagnostic script at `tests/diagnose_signal_biases.py` that, given one or more rollout JSONL paths, computes and prints:

  1. `verdict_bias`: marginal P(verdict=CORRECT) across all `solution_verifications[].counts`, broken out per-file and per-question. Compare to the oracle correct rate. Quantify the gap (positive bias = judge over-grants CORRECT).
  2. `parse_bias`: per sampling group (group_index in solver) compute the parse rate of `FINAL_ANSWER` and the per-group oracle solve rate. Report whether weak-temperature groups disproportionately fail to parse (which would confound `R_sep`).
  3. `unanimity_bias`: compare `verifier_pred_correct` vs `oracle_correct` for unanimous-CORRECT, unanimous-INCORRECT, and split votes; report precision/recall and a 2x2 confusion matrix per regime.
  4. `group_effects`: compute mean `oracle_correct`, mean verifier-correct rate, parse rate, and `R_sep` per sampling group; rank groups.
  5. Optional but high-value: also compute position bias if any `pairwise_judgments` rows are present (judge picking A vs B at random A/B positions).

The script must:
- Accept `--jsonl path1 [path2 ...]`.
- Print a clean text report to stdout AND write a Markdown summary to `outputs/diagnostics/signal_biases.md` (create directory).
- Be runnable as `python tests/diagnose_signal_biases.py --jsonl <paths>` and from `python -m tests.diagnose_signal_biases`.
- Tolerate older JSONL schemas (some files may lack `oracle`, `solution_verifications`, or `pairwise_judgments`); skip missing fields cleanly.

After implementing the script:
- Run it on the strongest existing artifact: `outputs/pairwise_rollouts_debug/samples_functional_smoke_50_answer_verify.jsonl` AND `outputs/pairwise_rollouts_debug/samples_functional_smoke_10_answer_verify.jsonl`. Commit the resulting `outputs/diagnostics/signal_biases.md` so the planner can read concrete numbers from the handoff.
- Quote the headline findings in your handoff `## Notes` (e.g. 'judge over-grants CORRECT by +X%pp; weak group has Y%pp lower parse rate; non-unanimous accuracy is Z% vs unanimous W%').
- DO NOT execute any rollout, training, or remote-GPU work. Pure offline analysis on artifacts already in the repo.

Lint/test discipline:
- `ruff check .` must still pass after your changes (the repo CLAUDE.md flags it as the lint command).
- Keep the script self-contained (stdlib + only what is already available; the project uses Python with `pyproject.toml`).
acceptance: tests/diagnose_signal_biases.py exists and runs cleanly via `python tests/diagnose_signal_biases.py --jsonl outputs/pairwise_rollouts_debug/samples_functional_smoke_50_answer_verify.jsonl outputs/pairwise_rollouts_debug/samples_functional_smoke_10_answer_verify.jsonl`.
outputs/diagnostics/signal_biases.md is committed and contains numerical results for verdict bias, parse bias, unanimity bias, and per-group effects.
Handoff `## Notes` quotes the headline numbers (verdict bias %pp, parse-rate per group, unanimous vs non-unanimous accuracy, group ranking by R_sep).

tasks.name: rl-loop-smoke
tasks.scopedGoal:
Drive a real self-play GRPO loop on the project's cloud GPU box (NOT inside the cloud-agent VM) and produce committed evidence that GRPO is improving the solver across cycles. Use the local-vLLM Llama-3.1-8B setup that `outputs/report5.md` already validates.

Execution substrate (read this carefully — your VM has NO GPU; you MUST run via SSH):
- The project owner's GPU box is reachable through SSH at `$SSH_HOST` as `$SSH_USER` with `$SSH_PASS` (use `sshpass -p "$SSH_PASS"` if interactive auth is needed; if `sshpass` isn't installed, `apt-get install -y sshpass` works in the cloud-agent VM).
- The remote workspace already contains a clone of this repo at `$REMOTE_WORKSPACE_PATH`. SLURM is available via `$SLURM_PARTITION`, `$SLURM_GRES`, `$SLURM_ACCOUNT`.
- Treat all four secrets (`SSH_HOST`, `SSH_USER`, `SSH_PASS`, `REMOTE_WORKSPACE_PATH`) as already present in your environment; do NOT echo them, do NOT paste them into commit messages, but DO use them via shell variable expansion.
- All GRPO/vLLM work happens on the remote box. Your branch on this side carries the *evidence* (small JSONLs, markdown reports, summary numbers), not the model weights.

What to actually do:
1. From the cloud-agent VM, `git push` your current branch and on the remote box `git fetch && git checkout <branch>` so the remote runs the same code.
2. Bring up vLLM on the remote box (GPU 1) serving `meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct` exactly as `outputs/report5.md` describes (`vllm serve ... --port 8001 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.45`). Wait for it to be healthy on `127.0.0.1:8001`.
3. On GPU 0 of the remote box, run the closed-loop self-play GRPO driver: `python -m grpo_math.self_play.run_self_play_grpo_loop --rollout_config grpo_math/configs/pairwise_rollouts_llama31_8b_vllm_single_verify_fast.yaml --train_config grpo_math/configs/train_pairwise_verdict_llama31_8b_lora_local_teacher_smoke_trl.yaml --cycles 2 --max_steps 1 --max_train_samples 8 --max_eval_samples 2 --log_rollouts_to_wandb`.
   - `cycles=2` is the cap to stay inside cloud-agent runtime; one cycle is roughly the rollout-then-train block proven in report5. Increase only if there is comfortable headroom and the first cycle finishes well under 30 minutes wall.
   - `WANDB_API_KEY` should fall through from the existing env (the project uses `WANDBKEY` aliased to `WANDB_API_KEY` per report5).
4. Pull back the cycle artifacts:
   - Each cycle's `samples.jsonl` is small (≪1MB even at ~50 questions × 10 solutions) — copy `outputs/self_play_grpo_loop/<TAG>/cycle_*_samples.jsonl` into this repo at `outputs/self_play_grpo_loop_smoke/cycle_*_samples.jsonl`.
   - Do NOT pull model checkpoints. They are too large; keep them on the remote box.
5. Run the project's existing analyzer on each pulled cycle JSONL: `python tests/analyze_rollout_results.py outputs/self_play_grpo_loop_smoke/cycle_001_samples.jsonl` and the same for cycle_002. Capture the parse rate, oracle solve rate, R_sep mean, R_sep positive fraction, and verifier-vs-oracle precision/recall per cycle.
6. Write a report at `outputs/self_play_grpo_loop_smoke/report.md` answering:
   - Did the solver oracle solve rate improve cycle-over-cycle (cycle_001 → cycle_002)? Quote both numbers.
   - Did `R_sep` move? Did the strong/weak gap collapse or hold?
   - Did training metrics (`grpo/train/loss`, `grpo/train/grad_norm`, `grpo/train/reward`, `grpo/train/reward_std`, `grpo/train/kl`, `grpo/train/entropy`) look stable, or did they diverge / collapse?
   - One paragraph honest assessment: 'RL is working / RL is not working / inconclusive at this scale, because <reason>'.
7. Commit the pulled JSONLs, the report, and any small TRL trainer_state.json snippets you copied back, but NOT model weights or anything > a few MB.

If SSH/SLURM blocks you (no GRES, queue saturated, network drop, vLLM fails to start, OOM at 8B), STOP, do not retry blindly more than twice; instead write `outputs/self_play_grpo_loop_smoke/report.md` documenting exactly what failed and at which step, then hand off `Status: blocked` so the planner can replan around it. Do not invent numbers.

Quality floor:
- Honest reporting > optimistic reporting. If RL did not improve solver, say so plainly with the numbers.
- No placeholder TODOs in the report — every section answered with what you actually observed.
- Don't push or merge to main; keep everything on your branch.
acceptance: outputs/self_play_grpo_loop_smoke/report.md exists, includes per-cycle parse rate, oracle solve rate, R_sep mean and positive fraction, verifier accuracy, and a final paragraph stating whether RL is working with citation to the numbers above. If blocked end-to-end on env, the report still exists and documents the failure mode.
Cloud-agent runtime stays under cap; in-flight remote SLURM jobs are cancelled or short enough not to leak.
